pinyin: yuǎn zài tiān biān, jìn zài yǎn qián
gloss: Distant in the sky, close at hand; often refers to things that seem far away but are actually near.
teaser: Ever felt that something you want is just out of reach?
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever felt that something you want is just out of reach?[break 1s]The phrase is: 远在天边，近在眼前, yuǎn zài tiān biān, jìn zài yǎn qián.[break 0.5s]远 (yuǎn) - distant[break 0.5s]在 (zài) - at[break 0.5s]天 (tiān) - sky[break 0.5s]边 (biān) - edge[break 0.5s]， (,) - (comma)[break 0.5s]近 (jìn) - near[break 0.5s]在 (zài) - at[break 0.5s]眼 (yǎn) - eye[break 0.5s]前 (qián) - front[break 0.5s]Full idiom again: 远在天边，近在眼前 means literally 'Distant in the sky, close at hand.' Figuratively, it refers to the idea that what we desire or seek may seem far away but is actually very close to us.[break 1s]Here’s the story behind it:[break 1.5s]This idiom originates from ancient Chinese literature, where it was often used to describe aspirations or dreams that feel unattainable. People would express how their goals seemed as distant as the horizon yet were much closer than they realized. It highlights the irony of human perception regarding our desires and achievements.[break 1.5s]Example 1: 这份工作可能远在天边，但其实你离它很近。 [break 1s]This job may seem far away, but actually, you're very close to it.[break 1s]Example 2: 他想要的成功，远在天边，近在眼前。 [break 1s]The success he desires seems distant, yet it’s right in front of him.[break 1s]Example 3: 你的梦想远在天边，但努力后就会发现它很近。 [break 1s]Your dream seems far away, but after working hard, you'll find it's quite near.[break 1s]So remember, 远在天边，近在眼前 means that what seems far might actually be close.
